newsitem.title: USA: Ciampi says G7 appreciates Italy's progress.
newsitem.headline: Ciampi says G7 appreciates Italy's progress.

text.p: The Group of Seven on Sunday praised Italy's progress in reducing its budget deficit and lowering inflation, but noted the slow pace of its recovery, Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said.

At a news conference following a meeting of the world's seven leading industrial nations, Ciampi said Italy's partners expressed confidence that it will continue to pursue efforts to contain the deficit.

"The G7 partners expressed appreciation for the curtailment of inflation, the solidity of the Italian economy, but also noted the slow rhythm of its recovery compared to the other European countries," Ciampi said. "They expressed confidence that Italy will continue its structural efforts to reduce the budget deficit, and that there might eventually be a more expansive monetary policy," he said.

Ciampi dismissed criticism that Italy will be a couple of tenths of a point short of the 3 percent deficit-to-GDP target needed by year-end to be in the first group of countries taking part in the European single currency.
"There has been great appreciation for the very strong reduction of the budget deficit ... There has been enormous progress. The judgment (of the G7) is positive."
The European Commission has forecast a 3.2 percent deficit/GDP ratio for Italy in 1997, while the International Monetary Fund, in its World Economic Outlook, sees a 3.3 percent ratio.

"These are only forecasts. We have accelerated the process of reducing the deficit by bringing forward to 1997 the 3.0 percent goal we had initially set for 1998. This acceleration brought advantages, increasing the country's credibility and accelerating the drop in interest rates," Ciampi said.

The forecasts "reflect the fact that in order to bridge the gap and reach the target by year-end we have had to take one-off budget measures. That 'pontoon' will be replaced by an iron bridge," Ciampi said.
Both the IMF and the European Commission have asked Italy for more structural deficit cutting measures.
